Types: enum GroupState { Open, Closed, Recurred }; struct Group { layer: String, title: String (the newest finding's raw title), key: String (normalize_title), state: GroupState, findings: usize, oldest_open_ts: Option<String>, newest_finding_ts: String, latest_close: Option<serde_json::Value>, features: Vec<String> }; struct Ledger { groups: Vec<Group> } with a pure fn Ledger::from_rows(rows: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Ledger and an IO fn Ledger::load(root: &Path) -> Option<Ledger> that reads .bee/backlog.jsonl the way feedback.rs fix_at_load does. cells.title: Fold fix-at backlog rows into one ledger
cells.action: Implement CONTEXT.md D1. Create verbs/fix_at.rs and register it in verbs/mod.rs. Types: enum GroupState { Open, Closed, Recurred }; struct Group { layer: String, title: String (the newest finding's raw title), key: String (normalize_title), state: GroupState, findings: usize, oldest_open_ts: Option<String>, newest_finding_ts: String, latest_close: Option<serde_json::Value>, features: Vec<String> }; struct Ledger { groups: Vec<Group> } with a pure fn Ledger::from_rows(rows: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Ledger and an IO fn Ledger::load(root: &Path) -> Option<Ledger> that reads .bee/backlog.jsonl the way feedback.rs fix_at_load does. Layers: fix-at:check, fix-at:architecture, fix-at:rejudge. Rules per D12: a close is a row whose type or kind is backlog-closed; a close carrying a fix-at layer matches only its own layer, a close with no fix-at layer matches every layer by normalize_title; a finding is an is_finding_row row on a fix-at layer. A group is Closed when its latest matching close is newer than its newest finding; Recurred when a finding is newer than a close; Open when it never closed. oldest_open_ts is the oldest finding ts in the current epoch (after the latest close). Add Ledger::current_epoch_feature(layer, title) -> Option<String> with the exact semantics of backlog.rs current_epoch_finding_feature, and make that backlog.rs function a thin caller of it (or replace its call in close.rs). Rebuild feedback.rs fix_at_load on Ledger::from_rows, keeping every prose_load key and value identical (fix_at_check_open, fix_at_architecture_open, fix_at_closed count groups as today; Recurred counts as open). Existing tests in feedback.rs, backlog.rs and close.rs must stay green unchanged; if one goes red because of the D12 layer rule, stop and report it. Also run cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- feedback and -- backlog and quote both counts. Write no code comment of any kind. Never edit .bee/*.json or .bee/*.jsonl by hand. Run only the cell's verify filter, never the full suite. cells.title: Add the fix-at close, verify, next and promote verbs and the upkeep kind
cells.action: Implement CONTEXT.md D7, D8, D9 and the D9 refinement. bee backlog fix-at <close|verify|next|promote> dispatched from backlog.rs try_native (a fix-at arm with a sub-match, like pbi). close: flags layer, title, guard, guard-cmd, red-proof, commit, kept; refuses unknown or already Closed groups, empty guard/guard-cmd/red-proof (kept replaces all three only for fix-at:rejudge); runs guard-cmd with sh -c from the repo root with a 600 s timeout and refuses on non-zero exit, quoting the tail of its output; on success appends a backlog-closed row {ts,type,title,detail,severity P3,layer,feature,guard,guard_cmd,red_proof,commit} via a new row builder (backlog_finding_row keeps its seven keys). bee backlog add refuses --type backlog-closed when --layer starts with fix-at: and names the fix-at close verb. verify: skips a Closed group with no guard_cmd and lists it as unverifiable (a kept rejudge, a legacy hand close); re-runs every other Closed group's guard_cmd; a non-zero exit appends a finding row (same layer and title, detail 'guard went red: <cmd>') and the verb exits 1; it logs one audit row of kind fix-at-upkeep (add the kind to audit.rs KINDS). next: prints the top group (Recurred, then findings desc, then oldest) with --json. promote: files one proposed PBI titled 'Guard: <title>' through the same writer the pbi add verb uses, refusing while a PBI whose title starts with 'Guard: ' is proposed or in flight. Session takeup in work.rs runs promote silently after sweep_unfiled when debt exists. Session takeup reads and writes through the control root. upkeep_group.rs gains Kind::FixAt (name fix-at, audit kind fix-at-upkeep, JSON item skill null and invoke 'bee backlog fix-at verify, then bee backlog fix-at promote', text run line the same command pair, present when the ledger has any group, due when a Closed group exists and no fix-at-upkeep row is younger than 7 days); extend the --kind parse and refusal. Add registry_payload.json entries backlog.fix-at.close, backlog.fix-at.verify, backlog.fix-at.next, backlog.fix-at.promote with schemas and examples, and the router shape strings. The new flag names (guard, guard-cmd, red-proof, commit, kept) grow the pinned flag vocabulary: bump PINNED_FLAG_COUNT in catalog.rs by the number of truly new names after the reuse check the test demands, and put the reason in the commit body. Also run cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test registry_contracts, --bin bee -- distinct_flag_vocabulary and --bin bee -- upkeep, and quote each count.
